title: Cymatics experiment in the King's Chamber produces the Eye of Horus

tellings.quote: actually um did some experiments alongside some other scientists in the king's chamber where they they stretched a membrane uh over the uh sarcophagus of the king's chamber like a cladney plate like a simatic plate and they put Egyptian sand on the plate and they sent vibrational frequencies that match the the frequency of the king's chamber through it and it turned into the eye of Horus.

plain: The claim is that scientists in the King's Chamber, the stone room at the heart of Egypt's Great Pyramid, stretched a membrane over the granite box called the sarcophagus. They used it like a Chladni plate, a surface that turns sound into visible patterns as sand settles on it. They sprinkled Egyptian sand on it, played the chamber's own vibrating frequency through it, and the sand formed the Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian eye symbol. A guest named Jay Anderson tells this on Michels's show and says it came from a man named David Elkington, who he says took part in the experiments. If true, it would suggest the chamber was built with sound in mind.
